en.caption: Erebos's Quests
rows: Capture a hero who came back to Theros as a Returned and send them back to the Underworld.
Find out why those who die in a coastal village never arrive in the Underworld, and why the village is haunted by eidolons.
Protect those who attend the funeral of a village elder in the hills near Akros, where minotaurs have disrupted recent burials.
Investigate an alchemist who claims to have transmuted lead into gold—but who might somehow be stealing it from the Underworld.
Refute the claim of a priest of Heliod who is said to be immortal because of the sun god's blessing.
Take an aging champion of Iroas who has pledged their soul to Erebos in exchange for a glorious death on one last foray into the wild lands.

en.caption: Karametra's Divine Schemes
rows: Karametra's statues have covered their faces as if in despair, and nothing will grow. No one seems to know what has caused the god of fertility to withdraw her blessings from the world, but the problem must be solved if life is to endure.

Karametra judges that mortals have over produced and moves to cull populations. She creates new plant species that feed on mortals, while her followers act oddly, running off to join bloody revels or sacrificing each other in the fields. How many must die before balance is restored?
Karametra's civilizing influence infringes on the territory and freedom of other nature gods, and so Nylea and Pharika band together to reduce her power.

Karametra bestows her gifts on a wild cultist or minotaur champion trying to encourage her older, more bloodthirsty worship. The faith takes hold, causing the god to make vicious demands of her followers.
en.name: Karametra's Divine Schemes

en.caption: Leonin and the Gods
rows: I'm amused by the antics of the gods and their earnest, but ultimately deluded, mortal champions, and I feel smugly superior in my detachment.
The meddling of the gods in mortal affairs makes me angry and bitter. I wish they would just leave us all alone!
I view the gods as worthy adversaries—incredibly clever and well-prepared to play a long game but ultimately doomed to lose their games.
I'm certain every bad thing that happens can ultimately be blamed on the gods, but I roll my eyes at each new twist of fate and try to get on with my life.
I wish that I could be as naive as humans and other mortals who actually think the gods are looking out for them. I miss that kind of innocence.
I don't talk about it among other leonin, but I actually revere the gods and try to please them by my actions.
en.name: Leonin and the Gods

texts.fr: Les léonins et les dieux
Attitude
Les pitreries des dieux et de leurs champions mortels sincères mais finalement abusés m'amusent, et mon détachement me donne un sentiment satisfait de supériorité.
L'ingérence des dieux dans les affaires mortelles me rend furieux et amer. J'aimerais qu'ils nous laissent tous tranquilles !
Je vois les dieux comme des adversaires dignes de ce nom, incroyablement intelligents et bien préparés à jouer sur le long terme, mais finalement condamnés à perdre leurs jeux.
Je suis certain que tout malheur peut finalement être imputé aux dieux, mais je lève les yeux au ciel à chaque nouveau caprice du destin et j'essaie de poursuivre ma vie.
J'aimerais être aussi naïf que les humains et les autres mortels qui pensent vraiment que les dieux veillent sur eux. Cette innocence me manque.
Je n'en parle pas parmi les autres léonins, mais je révère en réalité les dieux et j'essaie de leur plaire par mes actes.
